Northern Flicker has no elongated central tail feathers, unlike the dramatically extended tail streamers of the Scissor-tailed Flycatcher.
Acadian Flycatcher: Acadian Flycatcher has a distinct olive-green crown that contrasts sharply with its grayish-olive upperparts.
Acadian Flycatcher has a pale yellow throat and belly that is brighter and more uniform than the duller, buffier underparts of the Least Flycatcher.
Acadian Flycatcher shows a prominent white eyering that forms a complete, unbroken circle around the eye, unlike the broken or faint eyering of the Yellow bellied Flycatcher.
Acadian Flycatcher has a relatively long, slender bill with a dark upper mandible and pale lower mandible, whereas the Great Crested Flycatcher has a stouter, heavier bill.
Acadian Flycatcher displays two bold, pale wingbars on otherwise dusky wings, while the Olive sided Flycatcher shows only one narrow, indistinct wingbar.
Acadian Flycatcher has a longer tail than the Least Flycatcher, extending noticeably beyond the folded wingtips when perched.
Acadian Flycatcher lacks the rufous wing patches seen in the Vermilion Flycatcher.
Acadian Flycatcher has no rufous or chestnut coloration on the crown or nape, unlike the Red eyed Vireo.
Acadian Flycatcher shows no streaking on the breast, distinguishing it from the heavily streaked breast of the Song Sparrow.
Acadian Flycatcher has plain, unstreaked olive-gray upperparts, unlike the boldly streaked back of the Tennessee Warbler.
Acadian Flycatcher lacks the bright yellow spectacles and black mask of the Prothonotary Warbler.
Acadian Flycatcher has no wing coverts marked with rufous or cinnamon, unlike the Brown Creeper.
Acadian Flycatcher does not have the bold black-and-white head pattern of the Black capped Vireo.
Acadian Flycatcher has no white outer tail feathers visible in flight, unlike the Eastern Towhee.
Acadian Flycatcher lacks the rusty wing patches and strong facial pattern of the Red winged Blackbird.
Acadian Flycatcher has no crest, distinguishing it from the Crested Auklet.
Acadian Flycatcher shows no yellow edging on wing feathers, unlike the Yellow warbler.
Acadian Flycatcher has no white throat patch bordered by black like the Gray Catbird.
Acadian Flycatcher lacks the thick, hooked bill and dark hood of the Loggerhead Shrike.

Acadian Flycatcher shows no rufous wing linings like the Olive sided Flycatcher.
Acadian Flycatcher has no white-tipped tail feathers like the Blue Jay.
Acadian Flycatcher lacks the bold black-and-white face pattern of the Black billed Cuckoo.
Acadian Flycatcher has no yellow eyebrow contrasting strongly with a gray crown like the Philadelphia Vireo.
Great Crested Flycatcher: Great Crested Flycatcher has a prominent, erectile chestnut-brown crest that is absent in Least Flycatcher.
Great Crested Flycatcher has a bright lemon-yellow belly contrasting sharply with its olive-gray upperparts.
Great Crested Flycatcher displays a bold, blackish eye mask extending behind the eye, unlike the plain-faced Eastern Towhee.
Great Crested Flycatcher has a relatively large head and heavy bill compared to the petite Olive-sided Flycatcher.
Great Crested Flycatcher shows rusty-orange underwing coverts visible in flight, unlike the pale underwings of Acadian Flycatcher.
Great Crested Flycatcher possesses a long, rounded tail with faint rufous edging on outer feathers, unlike the short square tail of Yellow-bellied Flycatcher.
Great Crested Flycatcher has olive-gray upperparts without wingbars, distinguishing it from the two prominent white wingbars of Northern Flicker.
Great Crested Flycatcher exhibits a distinct pale yellow throat that contrasts with its gray breast, unlike the uniformly dark throat of Black-capped Vireo.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no eyering, whereas Warbling Vireo shows a faint but distinct pale eyering.
Great Crested Flycatcher lacks the bold white spectacles of Great Crested Flycatcher’s lookalike, the Gray Kingbird.
Great Crested Flycatcher has a stout, slightly hooked bill, unlike the slender, straight bill of Acadian Flycatcher.
Great Crested Flycatcher shows no streaking on its yellow belly, unlike the heavily streaked breast of Song Sparrow.
Great Crested Flycatcher has entirely olive-gray wings without spotting or barring, unlike the spotted wings of Spotted Catbird.
Great Crested Flycatcher displays no rufous crown patch like the Ruby-throated Hummingbird.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no red epaulets like the Red-winged Blackbird.
Great Crested Flycatcher lacks the bold black-and-white head pattern of the Loggerhead Shrike.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no chestnut wing patches like the Brown Creeper.
Great Crested Flycatcher shows no iridescence on its head or body, unlike the glossy plumage of Brewer Blackbird.

Great Crested Flycatcher lacks the deeply forked tail of Scissor-tailed Flycatcher.

Great Crested Flycatcher has no yellow wingbars like the Yellow Warbler.
Great Crested Flycatcher lacks the bold black-and-white striped head of the Pied-billed Grebe.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no inflatable throat pouch like the Brown Pelican.
Great Crested Flycatcher shows no white eye-ring and black mask combination like the Black-capped Vireo.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no rufous cap like the House Finch (not in list — instead: no rufous crown like the Cassin’s Finch, but not listed; use: no rufous crown like the Purple Finch).
Great Crested Flycatcher lacks the long, decurved bill of the Black-billed Cuckoo.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no barred flanks like the Louisiana Waterthrush.
Great Crested Flycatcher shows no streaked back like the Fox Sparrow.
Great Crested Flycatcher has no white outer tail feathers like the Eastern Towhee.

Least Flycatcher: Least Flycatcher has a pale grayish-olive upper body with no wing bars.
Least Flycatcher has a faint pale eye-ring that is less prominent than in Acadian Flycatcher.
Least Flycatcher lacks the bold yellow eyestripe found on Olive-sided Flycatcher.
Least Flycatcher has a relatively short, squared tail compared to the long, forked tail of Scissor-tailed Flycatcher.
Least Flycatcher shows no rufous crown patch like the Vermilion Flycatcher.
Least Flycatcher has plain, unstreaked underparts unlike the heavily streaked breast of Brown Thrasher.
Least Flycatcher lacks the bright yellow throat and belly of Yellow Warbler.
Least Flycatcher has no chestnut cap like the Red-eyed Vireo.
Least Flycatcher does not have the bold black-and-white head pattern of Black-capped Vireo.
Least Flycatcher has no wing bars, distinguishing it from Eastern Towhee which shows white wing patches.
Least Flycatcher lacks the strong facial pattern of Great Crested Flycatcher.
Least Flycatcher has no rufous tail edges like those seen in American Redstart.
Least Flycatcher has a small, slender bill without the heavy, hooked shape of Loggerhead Shrike.
Least Flycatcher shows no yellow lores like Yellow-bellied Flycatcher.
Least Flycatcher has no contrasting dark ear coverts bordered by pale feathers like Warbling Vireo.
Least Flycatcher lacks the bright red crest of Pileated Woodpecker.

Olive sided Flycatcher: Olive sided Flycatcher has a bold, contrasting white throat patch bordered by dark olive-gray on the sides of the breast.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a distinctive 'vested' appearance with dark olive-gray flanks sharply demarcated from a white belly and throat.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a thick, dark olive-gray band across each side of the breast that extends from shoulder to flank, unlike the uniformly streaked breast of Least Flycatcher.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a relatively large, blocky head with a flat crown, unlike the more rounded head of Acadian Flycatcher.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a short, squared-off tail that appears stubby in flight, unlike the longer, forked tail of Scissor tailed Flycatcher.

Olive sided Flycatcher has dark olive-gray ear coverts that blend seamlessly with the crown, unlike the contrasting pale lore and eye-ring of Acadian Flycatcher.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a broad, dark lateral throat stripe that meets at the lower throat, forming a 'V' shape not seen in Eastern Towhee.
Olive sided Flycatcher has plain, unmarked olive-gray upperparts without rufous tones, unlike the rufous rump and wings of Rufous Flycatcher.

Olive sided Flycatcher has a white throat that is cleanly separated from dark flanks by sharp edges, unlike the blurry, diffuse boundary in Olive sided Flycatcher’s closest relative, the Olive-sided Flycatcher (no duplicate — corrected: unlike the smudgy gray-brown flanks of Gray Kingbird).

Olive sided Flycatcher has no facial stripes, distinguishing it from the bold black-and-white head pattern of Loggerhead Shrike.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a pale mandible base that contrasts with its dark upper mandible, unlike the all-dark bill of Great Crested Flycatcher.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a relatively short, wide-based tail that lacks any rufous or cinnamon tones, unlike the rufous tail of Palm Warbler.
Olive sided Flycatcher has uniform olive-gray upperwing coverts with no spotting, unlike the spotted wing coverts of Spotted Catbird.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a white throat that extends fully to the upper breast without dusky mottling, unlike the faintly smudged throat of Gray Catbird.
Olive sided Flycatcher has no yellow on the head or face, unlike the bright yellow throat and eyebrow of Yellow breasted Chat.

Olive sided Flycatcher has a dark olive-gray rump that matches the back, unlike the contrasting rufous rump of Olive sided Flycatcher’s namesake confusion species — corrected: unlike the contrasting rufous rump of American Robin (not in list) — instead: unlike the pale gray rump of Sayornis phoebe.

Olive sided Flycatcher has a relatively heavy, straight culmen, unlike the decurved bill of Black billed Cuckoo.
Olive sided Flycatcher has no crest or tufts, unlike the prominent crest of Crested Auklet.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a pale grayish eye-ring that is narrow and indistinct, unlike the bold white eye-ring of Florida Jay.
Olive sided Flycatcher has olive-gray upperparts without iridescence, unlike the glossy purple-black plumage of Purple Finch.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a white throat that is uninterrupted by any dark markings, unlike the black throat patch of Black throated Sparrow.
Olive sided Flycatcher has plain, unbarred flight feathers, unlike the boldly banded remiges of Common Tern.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a dark olive-gray tail without any rufous edging, unlike the rufous-tipped tail feathers of Nashville Warbler.

Olive sided Flycatcher has a compact, stocky body shape with broad shoulders, unlike the slender, elongated silhouette of Olive sided Flycatcher’s distant relative — corrected: unlike the lanky frame of Brown Thrasher.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a pale grayish wash on the lores, not the stark white lores of White eyed Vireo.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a dark olive-gray crown without any contrasting cap color, unlike the chestnut cap of Brown Creeper.
Olive sided Flycatcher has a white throat that forms a clean, angular junction with the dark lateral breast patches, unlike the rounded, diffuse transition in Eastern Phoebe.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher: Scissor tailed Flycatcher has extremely long, deeply forked outer tail feathers that extend far beyond the wingtips in flight.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has pale pinkish underparts contrasting with a white belly and pale gray upperparts.

Scissor tailed Flycatcher has pale gray upperwing coverts with no wingbars, unlike the two bold white wingbars of Eastern Towhee.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a slender, black bill that is slightly upturned, unlike the stouter, straighter bill of Northern Flicker.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray rump that matches the back, unlike the contrasting cinnamon rump of Olive sided Flycatcher.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has white outer tail feathers with black central shafts, creating a striking pattern in flight.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has no eye-ring, distinguishing it from the prominent white eye-ring of Warbling Vireo.

Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray lores region, lacking the dark lores patch seen in Gray Catbird.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray auricular area without contrast, unlike the bold black-and-white head pattern of Black billed Cuckoo.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray upper tail coverts that blend seamlessly with the back, unlike the rufous upper tail coverts of Rufous Hummingbird.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a white vent that extends continuously from the belly to the undertail coverts, unlike the buffy vent of Yellow breasted Chat.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray scapular region with uniform coloration, unlike the scaled appearance of Sooty Albatross scapulars.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray nape without a crest, unlike the prominent crest of Crested Auklet.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray forehead that lacks any rufous or chestnut tones found in female Red headed Woodpecker.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray chin that merges smoothly into the white throat, unlike the black throat patch of Black throated Sparrow.
Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray upper breast that lacks streaks or spots, unlike the streaked breast of Fox Sparrow.

Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray interorbital region without dark markings, unlike the dark interorbital stripe of Black capped Vireo.

Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray nasal tuft area without feather elongation, unlike the elongated nasal bristles of Scissor tailed Flycatcher’s own namesake feature — wait, no: rephrase — Scissor tailed Flycatcher has no elongated nasal bristles, unlike the prominent bristles of Acadian Flycatcher.

Scissor tailed Flycatcher has a pale gray supraloral region that is smooth and unmarked, unlike the rufous supraloral patch of Rufous Hummingbird.
Vermilion Flycatcher: Vermilion Flycatcher is a small songbird with a strikingly bright red crown, throat, and underparts contrasting sharply with its dark brown upperparts.
Vermilion Flycatcher has a vivid scarlet-red belly and chest unlike the pale yellow or buff underparts of the Yellow-bellied Flycatcher.
Vermilion Flycatcher displays a bold black eye mask and dark brown cap that sharply borders its red face, unlike the plain gray head of the Least Flycatcher.
Vermilion Flycatcher possesses a short, broad, flat-topped crest that is often raised, distinguishing it from the smooth, uncrested crown of the Acadian Flycatcher.
Vermilion Flycatcher shows a clean white belly patch just below the red breast, absent in the uniformly red-breasted Scarlet Tanager.
Vermilion Flycatcher has narrow black wings with no wingbars, unlike the two prominent white wingbars of the Olive-sided Flycatcher.
Vermilion Flycatcher exhibits a relatively long, thin, black bill adapted for aerial insect capture, shorter and more delicate than the heavy, hooked bill of the Loggerhead Shrike.
Vermilion Flycatcher lacks any rufous or cinnamon tones on its flanks, unlike the warm rufous sides of the Red-eyed Vireo.
Vermilion Flycatcher has entirely dark brown upperparts without olive or greenish tones, unlike the olive-green back of the Warbling Vireo.
Vermilion Flycatcher shows no streaking on its red underparts, unlike the heavily streaked breast of the Song Sparrow.
Vermilion Flycatcher has a slender, upright posture when perched, distinct from the hunched, compact stance of the Gray Catbird.
Vermilion Flycatcher displays no white outer tail feathers in flight, unlike the conspicuous white tail corners of the Eastern Towhee.

Vermilion Flycatcher shows no yellow wingbars, unlike the bright yellow wingbars of the Magnolia Warbler.

Vermilion Flycatcher lacks a notched tail, unlike the distinctly notched tail of the Barn Swallow.

Yellow bellied Flycatcher has a prominent pale yellow eyering that forms a complete, unbroken ring around the eye.
Yellow bellied Flycatcher has olive-green upperparts with no strong rufous or gray tones, unlike the Rusty Blackbird or Gray Catbird.
Yellow bellied Flycatcher has two bold, pale yellow wingbars on otherwise dusky wings.
Yellow bellied Flycatcher has a short, narrow, dark bill with a pale lower mandible, contrasting with the thicker, all-dark bill of the Great Crested Flycatcher.
Yellow bellied Flycatcher has a relatively plain face without strong facial markings, unlike the boldly striped head of the Eastern Towhee.
Yellow bellied Flycatcher has a faint olive-gray auricular patch that lacks strong contrast, unlike the sharply defined black mask of the Black-capped Vireo.

Rose breasted Grosbeak has a black back without streaks or spots, unlike the heavily streaked back of the Louisiana Waterthrush.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a completely white belly and undertail coverts, unlike the buffy or streaked underparts of the Prairie Warbler.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a black tail with no rufous or chestnut tones, unlike the rufous tail of the Rufous Hummingbird.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a white wing stripe formed by median coverts, distinct from the yellow wing stripe of the Yellow Warbler.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a black face that includes the lores and ear coverts, unlike the pale-lored face of the Blue Jay.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a rose-red patch shaped like an inverted triangle on the breast, unlike the circular red patch of the Cardinal.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has white primary coverts creating a bold white flash in the wing, unlike the all-dark wings of the Black-billed Cuckoo.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a black chin and throat merging into the black breast sides, unlike the pale throat of the White-throated Sparrow.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a white belly unmarked by streaks or spots, unlike the streaked belly of the Lincoln Sparrow.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a black tail with white outer rectrices, unlike the entirely black tail of the American Crow.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a white eyering that is thin and complete, unlike the broken or absent eyering of the Warbling Vireo.
Rose breasted Grosbeak has a black back meeting the black wings without contrast, unlike the olive-green back of the Olive-sided Flycatcher.

California Gull: California Gull has a pale gray back and wings that are lighter than those of the Herring Gull.
California Gull has a yellow bill with a distinct black ring near the tip, unlike the uniformly yellow bill of the Ring-billed Gull.
California Gull has a white head in summer that lacks the dark hood of the Black-headed Gull.

California Gull has a clean white tail without the black band seen on the tail of the Laughing Gull.
California Gull has a relatively small, slender bill compared to the heavier bill of the Western Gull.
California Gull has a pale eye with a yellow orbital ring, unlike the darker eye of the Slaty-backed Gull.

California Gull has uniform pale gray upperparts without the dark mantle of the Great Black-backed Gull (not in list but contrast implied by absence; use instead: unlike the darker-backed Glaucous-winged Gull).

California Gull has a clean white underwing with gray primary tips, whereas the Heermann Gull shows extensive black underwing markings.
California Gull has no dark ear patch, distinguishing it from the Gray Catbird.
California Gull has a smooth, rounded head profile without the peaked crown of the Cedar Waxwing.
California Gull has plain gray upperparts without the barred back of the Brown Creeper.
California Gull has unmarked white underparts, unlike the streaked breast of the Song Sparrow.

California Gull has a medium-sized, compact body silhouette, smaller than the bulkier Western Gull.
California Gull has pale iris color, whereas the Red-eyed Vireo has a conspicuously red iris.

Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperwing coverts that match the mantle shade, unlike the Heermann Gull which has dark sooty-gray upperwings.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray rump that blends seamlessly with the back, unlike the contrasting white rump of the American Crow.

Glaucous winged Gull has no black on the tail, unlike the Black legged Kittiwake which has a black subterminal band on the tail.
Glaucous winged Gull has a rounded wingtip shape in flight, unlike the more pointed wingtips of the Arctic Tern.
Glaucous winged Gull has uniform pale gray upperwing feathers without barring or mottling, unlike the juvenile Pelagic Cormorant which shows heavy brown barring.
Glaucous winged Gull has a broad, blunt-tipped bill with a subtle gonys angle, unlike the sharply angled gonys of the Red faced Cormorant.

Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray back that is lighter than the slate-gray back of the Slaty backed Gull.
Glaucous winged Gull has a smooth, unmarked white head in breeding plumage, unlike the streaked head of the Dark eyed Junco.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray greater coverts that align closely in tone with the scapulars, unlike the contrastingly darker coverts of the Western Gull.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray tail without any dark banding, unlike the banded tail of the Ring billed Gull.
Glaucous winged Gull has a relatively small head in proportion to its body compared to the large-headed Western Gull.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperwing feathers that show no black or brown pigment, unlike the dusky-winged juvenile Brandt Cormorant.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale pinkish bill base that contrasts subtly with the black tip, unlike the uniformly yellow bill of the American Goldfinch.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray mantle that lacks warm brown tones, unlike the rufous-brown mantle of the Brown Creeper.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray wing stripe visible in flight that matches the back color, unlike the contrasting white wing stripe of the Barn Swallow.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray tertials without dark edges, unlike the narrowly edged tertials of the Olive sided Flycatcher.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray nape that merges smoothly into the crown, unlike the contrasting black crown of the Brewer Blackbird.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperparts without scaling or spotting, unlike the scaled appearance of the Spotted Catbird.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray rump that lacks any contrast with the tail, unlike the white rump patch of the Northern Flicker.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperwing coverts that lack pale edges, unlike the pale-edged coverts of the Gray Catbird.
Glaucous winged Gull has a pale gray back without streaking, unlike the heavily streaked back of the Fox Sparrow.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray scapulars that are uniform in tone, unlike the rufous-fringed scapulars of the Red winged Blackbird.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperwing feathers that lack any gloss or iridescence, unlike the glossy green upperparts of the Cape Glossy Starling.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperparts without any cinnamon or buff tones, unlike the buffy underparts and warm-toned wings of the Savannah Sparrow.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperwing coverts that lack dark shaft streaks, unlike the streaked coverts of the Song Sparrow.

Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperwing feathers that lack any rufous edging, unlike the rufous-edged wing feathers of the Eastern Towhee.
Glaucous winged Gull has pale gray upperparts that lack any yellow wash, unlike the yellow-tinged upperparts of the Yellow breasted Chat.
Heermann Gull: Heermann Gull has a uniformly dark gray to blackish body with no white on the back or wings, unlike the Herring Gull which shows extensive white on the rump and wingtips.

Herring Gull has a relatively large, heavy bill compared to the smaller-billed Ring-billed Gull.

Lincoln Sparrow has a narrow, dark eye line that extends just past the eye without curving downward, unlike the strongly downturned eye line of the Bachman's Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale buffy tinge on the flanks that blends gradually into the belly, unlike the sharply contrasting rufous flanks of the Fox Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a relatively long hind claw that is slender and curved, unlike the shorter, straighter hind claw of the Song Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale pinkish-buff tinge on the underwing coverts, unlike the whitish underwing coverts of the American Tree Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a finely vermiculated (wavy-line) pattern on the breast feathers, unlike the straight, parallel streaks of the Savannah Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale grayish lore that connects smoothly to the pale supercilium, unlike the dark lores of the Clay-colored Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a narrow, dark malar stripe that ends cleanly at the rear of the jaw, unlike the broad, smudgy malar stripe of the Swamp Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale cinnamon wash across the upperparts that is warmer than the cooler brown of the Song Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a faint, pale median crown stripe bordered by darker brown, unlike the bold, rufous-centered crown stripe of the Fox Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale grayish-brown iris that appears light in good light, unlike the dark brown iris of the Brewer's Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a delicate, finely streaked mantle with alternating narrow dark and pale feather edges, unlike the coarsely streaked mantle of the Grasshopper Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale buffy chin that merges seamlessly into the streaked throat, unlike the stark white chin of the White-throated Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a narrow, dark post-auricular stripe that is less prominent than the bold black stripe of the Black-throated Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale grayish-brown tail with faint rufous edging only on the outermost rectrices, unlike the uniformly rufous tail of the Rufous-crowned Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a smooth, unstreaked pale grayish belly, unlike the lightly streaked belly of the Clay-colored Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale buffy wash on the ear coverts that matches the supercilium, unlike the grayish ear coverts of the Chipping Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a slender, tapered primary projection that extends just beyond the tertials, unlike the shorter, blunter projection of the Swamp Sparrow.
Lincoln Sparrow has a pale cinnamon-buff wash on the upper breast that transitions smoothly into finer streaking, unlike the abrupt onset of heavy streaking in the Song Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp tailed Sparrow: Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a distinct pale yellow wash on the breast and flanks, unlike the unstreaked white breast of the White-throated Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows fine dark streaking on a buffy-brown back, contrasting with the plain gray-brown back of the Field Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow possesses a narrow, sharply defined black lateral throat stripe bordered by pale buff, unlike the broader and diffuse stripe of the Savannah Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a relatively short, pointed tail that is often held cocked, distinguishing it from the longer, rounded tail of the Song Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow displays a pale supercilium that tapers behind the eye without extending to the nape, unlike the bold, continuous white stripe of the White-crowned Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow exhibits a faint olive tinge on the upperparts, absent in the more uniformly brown upperparts of the Chipping Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale grayish face with no strong contrast, whereas the Lincoln Sparrow shows prominent rufous crown stripes and a well-defined eyering.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow lacks a distinct eyering, unlike the conspicuous white eyering of the Warbling Vireo.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no rufous cap, distinguishing it clearly from the rufous-capped Chipping Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale yellowish lores patch, not present in the darker, unmarked lores of the Swamp Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow features fine, dense streaking on the breast that converges toward the center, unlike the broader, more irregular streaks of the Fox Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a relatively plain, unstreaked throat, unlike the heavily streaked throat of the Grasshopper Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows a subtle olive wash on the scapulars, absent in the warm rufous scapulars of the Clay-colored Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow lacks a dark malar stripe, unlike the prominent black malar stripe of the Black-throated Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale buffy belly without spotting, unlike the spotted belly of the Vesper Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow displays a narrow, dark post-ocular line that does not connect to the nape, unlike the broad, connected gray nape of the Dark-eyed Junco.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a slender, conical bill with a pale pinkish base, unlike the thicker, all-dark bill of the Brewer Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no rufous wing panels, unlike the rufous-edged wing coverts of the American Redstart.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a soft, muted brown crown without streaking, unlike the boldly striped crown of the Harris Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow lacks a white eye-ring, distinguishing it from the prominent white eye-ring of the Ovenbird.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the auriculars, absent in the uniformly gray auriculars of the Slate-colored Junco.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no chestnut wing patches, unlike the chestnut wing coverts of the Brown Creeper.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a relatively long hind claw, but shorter than the extremely elongated hind claw of the Marsh Wren.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow displays no white outer tail feathers, unlike the conspicuous white outer rectrices of the Eastern Towhee.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a smooth, unstreaked nape, unlike the finely streaked nape of the Le Conte Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no bold facial pattern, unlike the stark black-and-white head of the Black-capped Vireo.

Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale yellowish wash across the breast that fades gradually into the flanks, unlike the sharp demarcation between white breast and rufous flanks in the Rose-breasted Grosbeak.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow lacks any red or orange plumage, distinguishing it from the bright orange throat of the Baltimore Oriole.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a uniform grayish-brown rump, unlike the rufous rump of the American Robin.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no white tail corners, unlike the white-tipped outer tail feathers of the Gray Catbird.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the undertail coverts, absent in the white undertail coverts of the White-throated Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow displays no wing bars, unlike the two prominent white wing bars of the Tennessee Warbler.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a relatively flat crown profile, unlike the peaked crown of the House Sparrow.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no dark ear patch, unlike the sharply defined black ear patch of the Black-headed Grosbeak.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a pale grayish eye-line that is less contrasting than the bold black eye-line of the Indigo Bunting.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow lacks a white throat patch, unlike the clean white throat of the Yellow-breasted Chat.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a soft, buffy-brown iris color, unlike the striking red iris of the Red-eyed Vireo.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow shows no yellow wing patches, unlike the bright yellow wing linings of the Magnolia Warbler.
Nelson Sharp-tailed Sparrow has a narrow, dark submoustachial stripe that is less pronounced than the bold black malar stripe of the Black-throated Blue Warbler.
Savannah Sparrow: Savannah Sparrow has a distinct yellow supraloral spot above the eye that is absent in Song Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a finely streaked breast with a central dark spot, unlike the unmarked breast of Field Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively short, conical bill compared to the longer, more decurved bill of Grasshopper Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish-brown crown stripe bordered by darker lateral crown stripes, unlike the solid gray crown of Chipping Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a buffy or pale yellowish wash on the face and throat, which is lacking in Lincoln Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively plain, unstreaked auricular region, whereas Fox Sparrow shows bold rufous and black streaking there.
Savannah Sparrow has a narrow, dark malar stripe that contrasts with its pale throat, unlike the broad, dark cheek patch of Vesper Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale supercilium that tapers behind the eye, while White-throated Sparrow shows a bold white stripe extending well beyond the eye.
Savannah Sparrow has dull brown upperparts with faint, narrow streaks, unlike the rich rufous and bold black streaking of Brown Thrasher.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively short tail that appears squared-off, whereas Tree Sparrow has a slightly notched tail.
Savannah Sparrow has no wing bars, distinguishing it from the two prominent white wing bars of Chipping Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale, unmarked belly, unlike the heavily streaked belly of Harris Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a narrow, dark lateral throat stripe that meets at the base of the bill, unlike the broad, solid black bib of Black-throated Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish lores patch, which is absent in Clay-colored Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively flat crown without a peaked appearance, unlike the distinct crest of Brewer Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish eyering that is incomplete behind the eye, whereas American Redstart has a complete, bold white eyering.
Savannah Sparrow has streaking that extends continuously from the back down onto the sides of the breast, unlike the isolated breast streaks of Song Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale, sandy-buff background color on the underparts, unlike the pinkish-buff underparts of Swamp Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively long, slender hind claw, longer than that of House Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has no rufous in the wing coverts, unlike the rufous-edged wing coverts of Fox Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a narrow, dark post-ocular stripe that does not broaden behind the ear, unlike the wide, dark post-auricular stripe of Seaside Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the bend of the wing, absent in Brewer Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively narrow, dark submoustachial stripe, whereas Nelson’s Sparrow shows a broader, more contrasting dark stripe below the moustache.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale grayish rump without rufous tones, unlike the rufous rump of Palm Warbler.
Savannah Sparrow has a plain, unstreaked nape, unlike the finely streaked nape of Lincoln Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish wash across the breast that blends smoothly into the throat, unlike the sharply demarcated white throat of White-throated Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively short, straight culmen without a noticeable bulge, unlike the swollen-based bill of Snow Bunting.
Savannah Sparrow has no white outer tail feathers, unlike the conspicuous white outer rectrices of White-crowned Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a subtle, diffuse olive wash on the scapulars, unlike the bright rufous scapulars of Fox Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale, straw-colored iris, whereas most other sparrows in the list have dark brown irises.
Savannah Sparrow has a narrow, dark lateral crown stripe that remains thin along its entire length, unlike the widening lateral crown stripe of Clay-colored Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the lower mandible, absent in Chipping Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively long, pointed primary projection extending beyond the tertials, unlike the shorter, blunter projection of Song Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale grayish-brown tail without rufous edges, unlike the rufous-fringed tail of Savannah sparrow’s close relative, Nelson’s Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a faint, pale median crown stripe that is narrower than the lateral stripes, unlike the broad, crisp white median stripe of White-crowned Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish wash on the auriculars that merges gradually into the throat, unlike the sharply defined gray auriculars of Dark-eyed Junco.
Savannah Sparrow has a relatively narrow, dark malar stripe that does not connect to the ear coverts, unlike the continuous dark cheek pattern of Black-throated Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the flanks that matches the breast wash, unlike the unstreaked, whitish flanks of Field Sparrow.
Savannah Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the lores that connects to the supraloral spot, unlike the uniformly gray lores of Chipping Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow: Seaside Sparrow has a grayish-olive back with no strong streaking, unlike the heavily streaked back of the Song Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has a pale, nearly unmarked gray breast, contrasting with the heavily streaked breast of the Savannah Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has a distinct olive-gray nape that blends smoothly into the back, unlike the rufous nape of the Fox Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has a relatively short, conical bill adapted for salt marsh invertebrates, shorter than the longer, finer bill of the Grasshopper Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has dull yellowish lores, a feature absent in the plain-faced Field Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow lacks bold white wing bars, distinguishing it from the prominently wing-barred White-throated Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has a flat, uncrested head profile, unlike the peaked crown of the Chipping Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow shows no chestnut cap like the male House Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has no black bib or throat patch, unlike the male Brewer Blackbird.
Seaside Sparrow lacks the bright yellow underparts of the Yellow Warbler.
Seaside Sparrow has no white eye-ring, unlike the distinct white eye-ring of the Ovenbird.
Seaside Sparrow has no rufous wing panels like those seen in the female Red-winged Blackbird.
Seaside Sparrow has no bold black-and-white head pattern like the male Indigo Bunting.
Seaside Sparrow has no rusty shoulder patches like the Rusty Blackbird.
Seaside Sparrow has no streaked flanks extending onto the belly, unlike the Lincoln Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has no buffy eyestripe contrasting sharply with a dark lateral throat stripe, unlike the Swamp Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has no bright orange throat like the male Baltimore Oriole.
Seaside Sparrow has no white outer tail feathers visible in flight, unlike the White-throated Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has no prominent white malar stripe like the Eastern Towhee.
Seaside Sparrow has no rufous crown like the female Brown Creeper.
Seaside Sparrow has no streaked crown, unlike the clearly streaked crown of the Clay-colored Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has no pale supercilium bordered by dark lines like the Nashville Warbler.
Seaside Sparrow has no yellowish-green upperparts like the female Black-throated Blue Warbler.
Seaside Sparrow has no bold black-and-white facial pattern like the Loggerhead Shrike.
Seaside Sparrow has no pale blue-gray hood like the Gray Catbird.
Seaside Sparrow has no bright red crown like the male Cardinal.
Seaside Sparrow has no white throat patch like the male Bobolink.
Seaside Sparrow has no deeply forked tail like the Barn Swallow.
Seaside Sparrow has no glossy purple-black plumage like the Purple Finch.
Seaside Sparrow has no bright yellow eyebrow stripe like the Yellow-breasted Chat.
Seaside Sparrow has no rufous wing coverts like the female House Wren.
Seaside Sparrow has no black mask extending behind the eye like the male Black-capped Vireo.
Seaside Sparrow has no pale yellow underwing coverts visible in flight like the Palm Warbler.
Seaside Sparrow has no white-tipped tail feathers like the Northern Waterthrush.
Seaside Sparrow has no streaked undertail coverts like the Song Sparrow.
Seaside Sparrow has no bright white outer tail feathers like the Common Yellowthroat.
Seaside Sparrow has no pale blue-gray rump contrasting with brown back like the Blue Jay.
Seaside Sparrow has no black-and-white striped head like the Downy Woodpecker.
Seaside Sparrow has no bright yellow throat like the male Yellow Warbler.
Song Sparrow: Song Sparrow has a heavily streaked breast with a distinct central dark spot, unlike the uniformly plain breast of the Field Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a brown-streaked back with warm rufous tones on the wings and tail, unlike the grayish-brown unmarked back of the Chipping Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a rounded head with a prominent gray crown stripe bordered by darker lateral crown stripes, unlike the flatter-headed appearance of the Savannah Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a relatively long, rounded tail that is often held slightly cocked, unlike the shorter, square-tipped tail of the House Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has bold, dark streaks on a white or pale buff breast that converge toward a central dark spot, unlike the sparse, blurry streaks of the Lincoln Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a broad, dark malar stripe contrasting with a pale throat, unlike the indistinct or absent malar stripe of the Swamp Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a medium-length, conical bill that is dark gray with a paler base, unlike the smaller, finer bill of the Chipping Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a pale supercilium that extends behind the eye and contrasts with a dark eyestripe, unlike the duller, less contrasting eyebrow of the Fox Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has streaking that extends onto the sides of the breast and flanks, unlike the clean, unstreaked flanks of the White-throated Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a brownish-gray face with no strong facial pattern, unlike the bold black-and-white head stripes of the White-crowned Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a relatively short, notched tail with faint rufous edges, unlike the longer, deeply forked tail of the Barn Swallow.
Song Sparrow has a pale, unmarked belly below the streaked breast, unlike the heavily streaked belly of the Harris Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a dusky ear patch that blends gradually into the nape, unlike the sharply defined black ear patch of the Black-throated Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has wing feathers with distinct rufous edging, unlike the more uniform gray-brown wings of the Clay-colored Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a streaked back with noticeable rufous feather edges on scapulars, unlike the plain gray-brown back of the Vesper Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a pale lower mandible that contrasts with a dark upper mandible, unlike the all-dark bill of the Dark-eyed Junco.
Song Sparrow has a relatively large, robust body for a sparrow, unlike the slender, delicate build of the Palm Warbler.
Song Sparrow has a brown iris that appears dark at a distance, unlike the pale yellow iris of the Yellow-eyed Vireo.
Song Sparrow has a short, slightly decurved culmen, unlike the straight, stout culmen of the Rose-breasted Grosbeak.
Song Sparrow has a pale throat with fine dark streaks near the edges, unlike the solid white throat of the Eastern Towhee.
Song Sparrow has a grayish rump without strong contrast to the back, unlike the bright rufous rump of the American Robin.
Song Sparrow has a streaked nape that matches the back pattern, unlike the plain gray nape of the Tree Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a relatively long hind claw, visible in profile, unlike the shorter hind claw of the House Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a pale post-ocular spot that is subtle and not sharply defined, unlike the bold white eye-ring of the Ovenbird.
Song Sparrow has a brownish tail with faint rufous wash, unlike the black tail with white outer feathers of the Red-winged Blackbird.
Song Sparrow has a streaked breast that does not form a solid bib, unlike the solid black bib of the Brewer Blackbird.
Song Sparrow has a pale lores region that blends smoothly into the cheek, unlike the starkly contrasting black lores of the Black-throated Blue Warbler.
Song Sparrow has a brownish-gray tail without strong color contrast to the back, unlike the bright rufous tail of the Rufous Hummingbird.
Song Sparrow has a soft, diffuse breast streaking without sharp borders, unlike the crisp, narrow streaks of the Grasshopper Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a pale yellowish tinge on the lores and suborbital area, unlike the pure gray lores of the Chipping Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a relatively long, graduated tail with outer feathers slightly longer than central ones, unlike the even-length tail of the Savannah Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a brownish wing panel without strong contrast, unlike the bold white wing bars of the White-throated Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a streaked crown with no central stripe interruption, unlike the broken or double crown stripe of the Clay-colored Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a pale grayish-brown auricular region without strong patterning, unlike the black-and-white striped auricles of the White-crowned Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a brownish back with variable rufous feather edges but no olive tones, unlike the olive-green back of the Nashville Warbler.
Song Sparrow has a pale pinkish-buff wash on the breast sides, unlike the stark white breast sides of the Swamp Sparrow.
Song Sparrow has a medium-length tail that is neither deeply forked nor extremely short, unlike the long, deeply forked tail of the Scissor-tailed Flycatcher.
Song Sparrow has a streaked back with no strong spotting or scaling, unlike the scaled appearance of the Brown Creeper.
Song Sparrow has a pale supercilium that is widest behind the eye, unlike the narrow, evenly wide eyebrow of the Lincoln Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow: Tree Sparrow has a distinct chestnut-brown cap that contrasts sharply with its gray crown and nape.
Tree Sparrow has a small, neat black spot centered on its otherwise plain white breast.
Tree Sparrow has a two-toned bill: black upper mandible and yellow lower mandible.
Tree Sparrow has pale gray underparts that lack strong streaking or spotting compared to Song Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a rusty-brown patch on each shoulder, visible in flight and at rest.
Tree Sparrow has a clean gray rump that lacks the warm brown tones seen in Chipping Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has unstreaked, pale buffy flanks unlike the heavily streaked flanks of Savannah Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a relatively short, conical bill adapted for seed-eating, shorter than that of Fox Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a crisp white eye-ring that is more prominent than the faint eye-ring of Field Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a gray face with no dark lateral throat stripe, unlike the bold facial pattern of White-throated Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a plain gray nape without streaks or mottling, unlike the streaked nape of Lincoln Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a pale supercilium that extends behind the eye but does not curve downward like in Vesper Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has uniformly gray upperparts without rufous wing coverts, distinguishing it from Chipping Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no dark ear patch or malar stripe, unlike the strongly marked face of Black-throated Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a pale pinkish-brown tinge on its breast and sides, absent in the colder-toned White-crowned Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a relatively short tail with no white outer feathers, unlike the conspicuous white tail corners of Dark-eyed Junco.
Tree Sparrow has no streaking on its crown, whereas Grasshopper Sparrow shows fine central crown streaks.
Tree Sparrow has a smooth, unmarked gray cheek, contrasting with the heavily streaked cheek of Song Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a narrow, dark eyeline that stops short of the bill, unlike the continuous dark line in Swamp Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no rufous coloration on the head or face, unlike the rufous cap of Fox Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has a pale gray back with faint, indistinct streaking, less bold than the black-and-white streaking of White-throated Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no yellow on the lores or throat, unlike the bright yellow lores of Yellow Warbler.
Tree Sparrow has a compact, rounded head shape without a peaked crown like that of Brewer Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no dark malar stripe extending below the throat, unlike the sharp facial markings of Harris Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no chestnut wing bars, distinguishing it from the wing-barred pattern of American Goldfinch.
Tree Sparrow has no white outer tail feathers, unlike the boldly white-tailed pattern of Eastern Towhee.
Tree Sparrow has no rufous eyebrow stripe, unlike the prominent rufous supercilium of Clay-colored Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no dark central breast spot bordered by chestnut, unlike the larger, chestnut-ringed spot of House Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no streaked crown stripes, unlike the finely striped crown of Le Conte Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no bold black-and-white head pattern, unlike the stark contrast of White-crowned Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no yellowish wash on the breast, unlike the yellow-tinged breast of Yellow-breasted Chat.
Tree Sparrow has no rufous collar across the nape, unlike the distinct nape band of Fox Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no dark streaks converging on a central breast spot, unlike the dense streaking of Song Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no pale blue-gray hood, unlike the hooded appearance of Gray Catbird.
Tree Sparrow has no white wing patches, unlike the large white wing patches of Red-winged Blackbird.
Tree Sparrow has no streaked auriculars, unlike the dark-streaked ear coverts of Swamp Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no olive-green cast on upperparts, unlike the olive tones of Nashville Warbler.
Tree Sparrow has no rufous rump, unlike the bright rufous rump of Fox Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no dark lateral throat stripe meeting at a point, unlike the sharp V-shaped throat marking of White-throated Sparrow.
Tree Sparrow has no pale yellow wash on the belly, unlike the yellow-bellied appearance of Yellow Warbler.
Vesper Sparrow: Vesper Sparrow has a distinct white outer tail feather visible in flight, unlike the uniformly dark tails of most other sparrows including Song Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow displays a fine, crisp white eye-ring that contrasts sharply with its brownish face, unlike the incomplete or absent eye-rings of Field Sparrow and Chipping Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow possesses a small, neat chestnut patch on the crown, absent in nearly all other North American sparrows except Fox Sparrow (which has a larger, more diffuse rufous crown).
Vesper Sparrow shows plain, unstreaked grayish-brown upperparts without bold wing bars, distinguishing it from the heavily wing-barred White-throated Sparrow and Savannah Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a clean, pale buffy breast with no central spot or streaking, unlike the boldly spotted breast of Song Sparrow and the heavily streaked breast of Lincoln Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow exhibits a relatively long, notched tail with white edges, whereas Grasshopper Sparrow has a short, square tail without white margins.
Vesper Sparrow lacks lateral throat stripes, giving it a plain-faced appearance compared to the strongly striped head of White-crowned Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has pale pinkish-buff legs, contrasting with the darker gray or blackish legs of House Sparrow and Brewer Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no wing bars at all, unlike the two prominent pale wing bars of Chipping Sparrow and Clay-colored Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a narrow, pale supercilium that stops short of the nape, unlike the long, bold white stripe extending to the nape in White-throated Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow displays a smooth, unmarked pale throat, whereas Savannah Sparrow often shows faint lateral throat streaks.
Vesper Sparrow has a relatively slender, pointed bill adapted for insectivory, unlike the thicker, conical seed-cracking bill of House Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no streaking on the flanks, unlike the distinct flank streaks of Lincoln Sparrow and Swamp Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a pale, unmarked belly, contrasting with the finely streaked belly of Song Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow lacks any facial pattern beyond the eye-ring, unlike the bold black-and-white head stripes of White-crowned Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a soft, sandy-brown back without rufous tones, unlike the rich rufous back of Fox Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no yellow coloration anywhere on the body, distinguishing it from Yellow Warbler and Yellow-breasted Chat.
Vesper Sparrow has a relatively long hind claw, longer than that of Chipping Sparrow and Field Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow displays no malar stripe, unlike the distinct dark malar stripe of Black-throated Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a pale, buffy wash across the entire underparts, unlike the stark white underparts of Tree Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no rufous wing panels, unlike the rufous shoulders of female Red-winged Blackbird.
Vesper Sparrow has a plain, light grayish-brown rump, unlike the olive-green rump of Nashville Warbler.
Vesper Sparrow lacks any crest or tuft, unlike the prominent crest of Cedar Waxwing or Crested Auklet.
Vesper Sparrow has a short, thin, slightly decurved bill, unlike the stout, straight bill of Dark-eyed Junco.
Vesper Sparrow shows no eyestripe contrast—its supercilium is only subtly paler than the crown, unlike the stark white stripe of White-throated Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has uniformly pale, unmarked lores, unlike the dark lores of Swamp Sparrow and Lincoln Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow displays no streaking on the crown, unlike the fine central crown streaking of Song Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a relatively long, slender body shape with a flat-topped head profile, unlike the rounded head and compact body of House Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no yellow or orange on the face or throat, unlike the yellow throat of Yellow-breasted Chat or the orange face of Baltimore Oriole.
Vesper Sparrow has a pale, horn-colored lower mandible, unlike the black lower mandible of many warblers such as Yellow Warbler.
Vesper Sparrow lacks any white tail corners when perched, unlike the conspicuous white tail corners of Eastern Towhee.
Vesper Sparrow has a smooth, unstreaked nape, unlike the streaked nape of Lincoln Sparrow and Swamp Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no rufous edging on the flight feathers, unlike the rufous-edged secondaries of Pine Warbler.
Vesper Sparrow has a pale, unmarked auricular region, unlike the dark ear patch of Black-capped Vireo.
Vesper Sparrow displays no white wing patches in flight, unlike the large white wing patches of Red-winged Blackbird.
Vesper Sparrow has a pale, buffy post-ocular stripe that blends gradually into the nape, unlike the sharply defined white stripe of White-crowned Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow shows no dark lateral throat stripes, unlike the bold black stripes of Black-throated Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow has a pale, unmarked undertail coverts, unlike the streaked undertail coverts of Song Sparrow.
Vesper Sparrow lacks any facial mask, unlike the dark facial mask of Indigo Bunting and Painted Bunting.
White crowned Sparrow: White crowned Sparrow has a bold black-and-white striped crown with a central white stripe flanked by black stripes.
White crowned Sparrow has a plain gray face without an eye-ring, unlike the Gray Catbird which shows a dark cap and distinct eye-ring.
White crowned Sparrow has a pale gray breast and belly, contrasting with the heavily streaked breast of the Song Sparrow.
White crowned Sparrow has a long, rounded tail with no rufous edges, unlike the Savannah Sparrow which shows prominent rufous wing coverts and tail edges.
White crowned Sparrow has a yellow lores spot between the eye and bill, absent in the White throated Sparrow which lacks this feature despite similar crown patterning.

Red eyed Vireo: Red eyed Vireo has a plain gray crown that contrasts with its olive-green upperparts.

Red eyed Vireo has a dark gray to blackish lateral throat stripe bordered by white.
Red eyed Vireo has a relatively short, straight, and finely pointed bill adapted for gleaning insects.
Red eyed Vireo lacks wingbars entirely, unlike Blue headed Vireo which shows two distinct white wingbars.
Red eyed Vireo lacks any yellow on the head, distinguishing it from Yellow throated Vireo.
Red eyed Vireo has no white wing patches, unlike White eyed Vireo which shows prominent white wingbars.
Red eyed Vireo has no contrasting yellow under tail coverts, unlike Warbling Vireo which shows yellow there.
Red eyed Vireo has no rufous cap, unlike Philadelphia Vireo which shows a warm rufous crown.
Red eyed Vireo has no yellow wash on the flanks, unlike Red eyed Vireo’s close relative Black capped Vireo which shows more contrast in flank coloration.
Red eyed Vireo has no white throat patch, unlike Gray Kingbird which displays a stark white throat.
Red eyed Vireo has no streaking on the breast, unlike many sparrows such as Song Sparrow.

Red eyed Vireo has no bright yellow crown, unlike Yellow breasted Chat.
Red eyed Vireo has no orange or rufous wing panels, unlike Baltimore Oriole.

Red eyed Vireo has no chestnut wing coverts, unlike Brown Creeper.

Warbling Vireo has no olive-tinged crown, unlike Blue-headed Vireo which shows a bluish-gray crown with olive tinge.

Warbling Vireo has no dusky lateral throat stripe meeting at the base of the bill, unlike Red-eyed Vireo which shows converging dark lines on the throat.
Warbling Vireo has no yellow-washed lores, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which shows yellow extending into the lores.
Warbling Vireo has no contrasting gray cap set off by paler nape, unlike Blue-headed Vireo which shows a bluer cap against grayer nape.
Warbling Vireo has no pale yellow wash across the entire breast, unlike Philadelphia Vireo which often shows broader yellow-olive breast tone.
Warbling Vireo has no dark line through the eye, unlike Red-eyed Vireo which shows a subtle but consistent dark eye-line.
Warbling Vireo has no yellow on the bend of the wing, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which shows yellow in the lesser and median coverts.
Warbling Vireo has no olive-green mantle contrasting with duller wings, unlike Red-eyed Vireo which shows stronger mantle–wing contrast.
Warbling Vireo has no pale yellow supercilium, unlike Philadelphia Vireo which sometimes shows a faint yellowish eyebrow.
Warbling Vireo has no dusky ear coverts contrasting with pale throat, unlike Black-capped Vireo which shows stark ear–throat contrast.
Warbling Vireo has no greenish-yellow wash on upper tail coverts, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which shows yellow-green uppertail coverts.

Warbling Vireo has no yellow on the chin, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which shows solid yellow from chin to belly.
Warbling Vireo has no olive-tinged ear coverts, unlike Philadelphia Vireo which shows warm olive tones on ear coverts.
Warbling Vireo has no bluish tinge to the crown, unlike Blue-headed Vireo which shows a distinct cool-blue crown.
Warbling Vireo has no yellow on the lower belly, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which extends yellow to the undertail coverts.
Warbling Vireo has no dark moustachial stripe, unlike Red-eyed Vireo which shows a thin dark stripe below the eye.
Warbling Vireo has no yellow-tinged wing bars, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which shows yellow-edged wing coverts.
Warbling Vireo has no contrasting olive-green rump and uppertail coverts, unlike Red-eyed Vireo which shows greener rump and uppertail.
Warbling Vireo has no pale yellow throat bordered above by gray, unlike Yellow-throated Vireo which shows sharp gray–yellow boundary.
Warbling Vireo has no olive wash on the forehead, unlike Philadelphia Vireo which shows olive extending onto the forehead.
White eyed Vireo: White eyed Vireo has bright white irises that contrast sharply with its otherwise dark eyes, unlike Red eyed Vireo which has deep red irises.
White eyed Vireo displays bold yellow spectacles—bright yellow lores and eye-rings—that surround its white eyes, unlike Blue headed Vireo which lacks yellow lores.

White eyed Vireo has a yellowish wash on its flanks and undertail coverts, whereas Warbling Vireo shows no yellow on the flanks.
White eyed Vireo possesses a relatively short, stout, slightly hooked bill adapted for gleaning insects, unlike the longer, finer bill of Yellow throated Vireo.
White eyed Vireo exhibits a gray crown bordered by darker lateral crown stripes, unlike Red eyed Vireo which has an unmarked gray crown.
White eyed Vireo has a pale yellow throat and breast that fade into a whitish belly, unlike Black capped Vireo which has a starkly white throat and gray breast.
White eyed Vireo shows strong contrast between its olive back and bright yellow sides, unlike Blue headed Vireo whose sides are more washed-out and grayish.
White eyed Vireo has a blackish line through the eye bordered above by a yellow supercilium and below by a white malar stripe, unlike Red eyed Vireo which lacks the yellow supercilium.
White eyed Vireo displays a faint olive wash on the nape, whereas Warbling Vireo shows a more uniform grayish-olive nape without contrast.
White eyed Vireo has a clean white belly with no streaking or spotting, unlike Mourning Warbler which shows a heavily streaked breast.
White eyed Vireo shows no wing spots or markings beyond its two white wingbars, unlike Black and white Warbler which has bold black-and-white striped wings.
White eyed Vireo has a relatively long tail for a vireo, often held cocked upward, unlike Yellow throated Vireo which holds its tail level.
White eyed Vireo exhibits a pale yellow lower mandible contrasting with a dark upper mandible, unlike Red eyed Vireo which has an all-dark bill.
White eyed Vireo has a crisp, well-defined blackish eyeline extending from the bill to behind the eye, unlike Philadelphia Vireo whose eyeline is diffuse and indistinct.
White eyed Vireo shows a bright yellow patch on the bend of the wing visible in flight, unlike Red eyed Vireo which lacks any yellow wing patch.
White eyed Vireo has unstreaked olive upperparts, unlike Tennessee Warbler which shows fine greenish streaking on the back.
White eyed Vireo displays a white throat bordered sharply by yellow on the sides of the neck, unlike Blue headed Vireo whose throat is whiter and less bordered.
White eyed Vireo has a relatively large head in proportion to its body compared to other vireos like Warbling Vireo.
White eyed Vireo shows no rufous or chestnut tones anywhere on its plumage, unlike Red eyed Vireo which may show faint rufous tinges on the crown.
White eyed Vireo has a pale grayish wash on the auriculars (ear coverts), unlike Yellow breasted Chat which has solid black auriculars.
White eyed Vireo exhibits a narrow but distinct white tip on the outer tail feathers, unlike Red bellied Woodpecker which has broad white tail patches.
White eyed Vireo has uniformly olive-green scapulars without edging or contrast, unlike Magnolia Warbler which shows yellow-edged scapulars.
White eyed Vireo shows no facial stripes beyond the eyeline and supercilium, unlike Loggerhead Shrike which has bold black facial masks.
White eyed Vireo has a plain grayish rump matching the back color, unlike Palm Warbler which shows a rusty rump.
White eyed Vireo displays no wing spots or tertial edging, unlike Black throated Blue Warbler which has white wing spots and pale tertial edges.
White eyed Vireo has a smooth, unmarked olive mantle without streaks or scaling, unlike House Sparrow which shows heavy brown streaking.
White eyed Vireo shows a pale yellow wash across the entire breast, not just the throat, unlike Red eyed Vireo whose breast is mostly white.
White eyed Vireo has a relatively short primary projection—wings appear shorter beyond the tail—compared to Olive sided Flycatcher which has long, pointed primaries.
White eyed Vireo exhibits no sexual dimorphism in plumage; males and females look identical, unlike Painted Bunting where males are brightly colored and females are greenish.
White eyed Vireo has a pale yellow wash on the undertail coverts, unlike Gray Catbird whose undertail coverts are rufous.
White eyed Vireo shows no white tips on the greater coverts, unlike Northern Flicker which has prominent white wing patches.
White eyed Vireo has a compact, rounded wing shape in flight, unlike Scissor tailed Flycatcher which has extremely long, pointed wings.
White eyed Vireo displays no barring on the tail feathers, unlike Bay breasted Warbler which shows distinct tail barring.
White eyed Vireo has a pale yellow lower belly that blends smoothly into the white center, unlike Yellow Warbler whose entire underparts are rich yellow.
White eyed Vireo shows no streaking on the flanks, unlike Song Sparrow which has heavy dark streaking on pale flanks.
White eyed Vireo has a smooth transition from olive back to yellowish sides without a sharp demarcation, unlike Hooded Warbler which shows a crisp black hood bordering yellow underparts.
White eyed Vireo exhibits no white tail corners in perched view, unlike Eastern Towhee which shows bold white tail edges.
White eyed Vireo has a pale yellow wash extending onto the upper breast, unlike Red breasted Merganser which has a sharply defined rusty breast.
White eyed Vireo shows no iridescence on the crown or back, unlike Purple Finch whose crown and back shimmer with purple-pink sheen.
Yellow throated Vireo: Yellow throated Vireo has a bright, solid yellow throat that contrasts sharply with its white belly.
Yellow throated Vireo has two bold, white wing bars on otherwise olive-green wings.
Yellow throated Vireo has a distinct yellow eyering that fully encircles the eye.
Yellow throated Vireo has a yellow crown stripe bordered by black lateral crown stripes.
Yellow throated Vireo has olive-green upperparts without streaking or spotting.
Yellow throated Vireo has a relatively thick, slightly hooked bill adapted for insectivory.
Yellow throated Vireo lacks the black mask seen in Red eyed Vireo.
Yellow throated Vireo lacks the blue-gray head of Blue headed Vireo.
Yellow throated Vireo lacks the chestnut cap and white eyebrow of Philadelphia Vireo.
Yellow throated Vireo has yellow lores, unlike the dark lores of Warbling Vireo.
Yellow throated Vireo has yellow undertail coverts, whereas White eyed Vireo has white ones.
Yellow throated Vireo has no yellow on the breast—only the throat and crown stripe are yellow.
Yellow throated Vireo has a plain, unstreaked breast unlike the streaked breast of Tennessee Warbler.
Yellow throated Vireo has a longer, more robust bill than the slender-billed Yellow Warbler.
Yellow throated Vireo has olive-green tertials without rufous edging, unlike Mourning Warbler.
Yellow throated Vireo lacks the black-and-white head pattern of Black and white Warbler.
Yellow throated Vireo has no wing spots, unlike the spotted wing coverts of Bay breasted Warbler.

Yellow throated Vireo has no supercilium extending behind the eye, unlike the long white eyebrow of Nashville Warbler.
Yellow throated Vireo has no yellow on the flanks, distinguishing it from Yellow breasted Chat.
Yellow throated Vireo has no rufous wing patches like those of Ovenbird.
Yellow throated Vireo has no orange or red coloration anywhere, unlike Scarlet Tanager.
Yellow throated Vireo has no streaking on the back, unlike the streaked back of Song Sparrow.
Yellow throated Vireo has no facial stripes beyond the lateral crown stripes, unlike the complex face pattern of Loggerhead Shrike.
Yellow throated Vireo has no yellow on the forehead—only the crown stripe is yellow.
Yellow throated Vireo has no white throat—its throat is entirely yellow.
Yellow throated Vireo has no yellow wing patches, unlike the yellow wing patches of Magnolia Warbler.
Yellow throated Vireo has no black throat patch, unlike the black bib of Indigo Bunting.
Yellow throated Vireo has no rufous cap like that of Brown Creeper.
Yellow throated Vireo has no pale eye-ring contrasting with dark skin, unlike the prominent eye-ring of Gray Catbird.
Yellow throated Vireo has no white-tipped tail feathers, unlike the white outer tail feathers of Eastern Towhee.

Bay breasted Warbler: Bay breasted Warbler has a distinctive chestnut patch on the upper breast that contrasts sharply with its white belly.

Bay breasted Warbler has pale yellow underwing coverts visible in flight, unlike the white underwing coverts of the Magnolia Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler displays a narrow black submoustachial stripe below the white malar, unlike the broad black malar stripe of the Black-and-white Warbler.

Bay breasted Warbler has a pale pinkish-buff wash on the sides of the breast, absent in the stark white flanks of the Blackpoll Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler shows a dark ear patch bordered posteriorly by a white crescent, unlike the solid gray ear patch of the Gray Catbird.
Bay breasted Warbler has a slender, slightly decurved bill, unlike the straight, stout bill of the Pine Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler displays a chestnut patch on the upper breast that is more extensive and richer than the faint rusty wash on the breast of the Palm Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler has a dark line through the eye bordered above by a pale eyebrow stripe, unlike the indistinct or missing supercilium of the Worm-eating Warbler.

Bay breasted Warbler has a plain gray face without cheek patches, unlike the bold black-and-white facial pattern of the Black-and-white Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler exhibits a pale lemon-yellow throat, unlike the white throat of the Bay-breasted Warbler’s close relative the Black-throated Blue Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler has a soft brown back without olive tones, unlike the olive-green back of the Hooded Warbler.
Bay breasted Warbler shows a narrow black border along the rear edge of the wing, unlike the broad white wing patch of the Swainson’s Warbler.

Bay breasted Warbler exhibits a pale grayish-brown tarsus, unlike the pinkish tarsus of the Louisiana Waterthrush.
Bay breasted Warbler has a pale grayish-brown base to the lower mandible, unlike the bright orange base of the Baltimore Oriole’s bill.
Black and white Warbler: Black and white Warbler has bold, parallel black and white stripes covering its entire head and body, unlike the streaked or spotted patterns of most other warblers.
Black and white Warbler has a sharply defined black-and-white striped crown, whereas the Black-throated Blue Warbler has a solid blue crown.
Black and white Warbler lacks an eye ring, distinguishing it from the Warbling Vireo which shows a prominent pale eye ring.
Black and white Warbler has a straight, slender, slightly decurved bill adapted for probing bark, unlike the thicker, shorter bill of the Ovenbird.
Black and white Warbler shows no wing bars, whereas the Magnolia Warbler displays two distinct white wing bars.
Black and white Warbler has black-and-white striped flanks, while the Chestnut-sided Warbler has plain white flanks with chestnut flank patches.

Black and white Warbler has a black-and-white striped throat, whereas the Black-throated Green Warbler has a solid black throat patch.

Black and white Warbler has black-and-white striped undertail coverts, whereas the Pine Warbler shows plain yellow or buffy undertail coverts.

Black and white Warbler lacks a white eye ring, distinguishing it from the Red-eyed Vireo which displays a bold white eye ring.

Black and white Warbler shows no olive or yellow wash on the face, unlike the Palm Warbler which shows yellow spectacles and olive face.
Black and white Warbler has black-and-white striped ear coverts, unlike the Black-throated Blue Warbler which has solid blue ear coverts.
Black and white Warbler lacks a white wing patch, distinguishing it from the Swainson’s Warbler which shows a small white wing patch.
Black throated Blue Warbler: Black throated Blue Warbler has a solid black throat patch that contrasts sharply with its bright blue upperparts and white belly.
Black throated Blue Warbler has a distinct black face mask extending from the bill through the eye and down to the throat, unlike the uniformly gray face of the Black and white Warbler.
Black throated Blue Warbler displays vivid cobalt-blue upperparts, whereas the Cerulean Warbler shows softer sky-blue tones with less contrast.
Black throated Blue Warbler has crisp white underparts with no streaking, unlike the heavily streaked breast of the Nashville Warbler.
Black throated Blue Warbler features a bold black throat and upper breast separated by a clean white band, unlike the continuous black chest of the Black capped Vireo.
Black throated Blue Warbler shows a prominent white wing patch formed by large white edgings on the greater coverts, absent in the Black throated Green Warbler.

Bewick Wren has no olive-green upperparts, unlike the olive back and wings of the Worm-eating Warbler.

Bewick Wren has no yellow wash on the breast, unlike the yellow-tinged breast of the Nashville Warbler.

Carolina Wren has no spotting on the breast, unlike the spotted breast of the Spotted Catbird.

Marsh Wren has no red on the head or body, unlike the red crown of the Cardinal or red head of the Red-headed Woodpecker.
